subject.title: fix(plugins): allow user-installed and generated plugins to use api.runtime.state

question: Should persistent `api.runtime.state` storage be available to every explicitly activated native plugin, or only to plugins carrying a narrower provenance signal?
rationale: OpenClaw treats loaded native plugins as host-trusted code, but the current state API separately enforces installation provenance; automation cannot safely choose which model should become the permanent public plugin contract.

options.title: Trust activated native plugins
options.body: Remove the provenance-only state restriction and rely on existing activation, allowlist, ownership, and install-policy controls for every native plugin source.

options.title: Add explicit state trust
options.body: Retain a state capability gate but introduce one explicit trust signal that works consistently for managed installs, workspace development, and configured load paths.

options.title: Keep official-only access
options.body: Preserve the current restriction and change generated and community plugin workflows so they do not depend on persistent runtime state.

recommendation.title: Trust activated native plugins
recommendation.body: Remove the provenance-only state restriction and rely on existing activation, allowlist, ownership, and install-policy controls for every native plugin source.
